concepts.name: Layers of the Earth
concepts.summary: Name and describe the crust, mantle, outer core and inner core and say which are solid or liquid.

concepts.name: Mineral definition and properties
concepts.summary: Explain that a mineral is a naturally occurring, inorganic, crystalline solid with a definite chemical composition.

concepts.name: Three rock types
concepts.summary: Distinguish igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks by how they form.

concepts.name: Tectonic plates and boundaries
concepts.summary: Describe that the lithosphere is broken into moving plates and name the three boundary types and their motion.

concepts.name: Volcanoes and earthquakes basics
concepts.summary: Explain in simple terms that volcanoes release magma and earthquakes release energy from sudden movement on faults.

concepts.name: Weathering versus erosion
concepts.summary: Tell apart weathering as breakdown in place from erosion as removal and transport of material.

concepts.name: The rock cycle
concepts.summary: Describe how rocks change from one type to another through melting, cooling, weathering, burial and heat and pressure.

misconceptions.text: The Earth's mantle is a sea of liquid magma.
Any hard solid found in nature, such as coal or glass, counts as a mineral.
Weathering and erosion are the same thing.

concepts.name: Mineral identification tests
concepts.summary: Use hardness, streak, luster, cleavage and fracture to identify common minerals such as quartz, feldspar, calcite and mica.

concepts.name: Igneous texture and composition
concepts.summary: Relate grain size to cooling rate and classify rocks like granite and basalt by texture and felsic or mafic composition.

concepts.name: Clastic and chemical sedimentary rocks
concepts.summary: Identify common sedimentary rocks by grain size and composition and explain how compaction and cementation form them.

concepts.name: Metamorphic grade and foliation
concepts.summary: Identify metamorphic rocks by foliation and relate them to increasing heat and pressure.

concepts.name: Relative dating principles
concepts.summary: Apply superposition, original horizontality and cross-cutting relationships to order events in a simple rock sequence.

concepts.name: Earthquake waves and measurement
concepts.summary: Describe P, S and surface waves, locate focus and epicenter, and distinguish magnitude from intensity.

concepts.name: Volcano types and eruption styles
concepts.summary: Match volcano shapes and eruption styles to magma viscosity and gas content.

misconceptions.text: Color is a reliable way to identify a mineral.
Metamorphic rocks form when rock melts and recrystallizes.
The Richter magnitude and the shaking felt at a place measure the same thing.

concepts.name: Plate tectonic evidence
concepts.summary: Analyse fossil, rock-match, magnetic stripe and seafloor age evidence supporting plate motion.

concepts.name: Boundary settings and associated hazards
concepts.summary: Explain how each boundary type controls the distribution of volcanoes, earthquakes, trenches and mountain belts.

concepts.name: Fault types and stress
concepts.summary: Link tension, compression and shear to normal, reverse and strike-slip faults and recognise them in cross-section.

concepts.name: Folds and geologic structures
concepts.summary: Identify folds, dip and strike and describe how rock layers deform.

concepts.name: Reading geologic maps
concepts.summary: Interpret map units, contacts, symbols and outcrop patterns to infer structure and a cross-section.

concepts.name: Absolute dating and radiometric decay
concepts.summary: Use half-lives and parent-daughter ratios to calculate ages and choose suitable isotopes.

concepts.name: Weathering processes and soils
concepts.summary: Compare physical and chemical weathering and analyse how climate, rock type and time shape soils.

concepts.name: Depositional environments and facies
concepts.summary: Infer ancient environments from sedimentary structures, grain size and fossils.

misconceptions.text: Continents plow through the ocean floor as they move.
Radiometric dating of a sedimentary rock directly dates when its grains were deposited.
Contacts on a geologic map show the rocks' ages only, not their three-dimensional geometry.

concepts.name: Mantle convection and plate driving forces
concepts.summary: Analyse slab pull, ridge push and mantle convection as drivers of plate motion and assess hotspot models.

concepts.name: Magma generation and differentiation
concepts.summary: Explain how decompression, flux and heating produce melts and how crystallization changes magma composition.

concepts.name: Metamorphic facies and P-T paths
concepts.summary: Use mineral assemblages to infer pressure-temperature conditions and tectonic setting.

concepts.name: Stratigraphic correlation and sequence stratigraphy
concepts.summary: Evaluate correlations using fossils, markers and unconformities and interpret sea-level change in stratigraphic records.

concepts.name: Seismic hazard assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate fault slip rates, recurrence intervals and site effects to judge earthquake hazard.

concepts.name: Landscape evolution and geomorphic processes
concepts.summary: Explain how rivers, glaciers, slopes and tectonics together shape landforms and drainage patterns.

concepts.name: Geochemical and isotopic tracers
concepts.summary: Judge what oxygen isotopes, trace elements and radiogenic isotopes reveal about source, climate and process.

misconceptions.text: Plates are pushed along by convection currents dragging them like a conveyor belt, with no role for slab pull.
Unconformities and missing layers mean the stratigraphic record is a continuous clock.
Earthquake recurrence intervals are regular, so a quake is not due until the mean interval has passed.

concepts.name: Integrating multi-method geologic syntheses
concepts.summary: Combine structural, stratigraphic, geochemical and geochronologic data into a coherent regional history.

concepts.name: Competing tectonic model evaluation
concepts.summary: Weigh alternative models of orogeny, rifting and plume activity against field and geophysical evidence.

concepts.name: Uncertainty in geochronology
concepts.summary: Assess closure temperatures, decay constant errors and sample quality to judge the reliability of an age.

concepts.name: Designing field investigations
concepts.summary: Plan mapping and sampling campaigns that test specific hypotheses within logistical limits.

concepts.name: Deep time and mass extinction causes
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for large volcanism, impacts and ocean chemistry change as drivers of major biotic and environmental shifts.

concepts.name: Geohazard risk communication and mitigation
concepts.summary: Create hazard models and communicate probabilistic risk to guide land use and emergency planning.

concepts.name: Resource formation and geologic constraints
concepts.summary: Evaluate how tectonic setting, fluids and structure control where ore, hydrocarbons and groundwater accumulate.

misconceptions.text: A single well-dated sample settles the age of a geologic event.
One mass extinction cause must be correct, so competing hypotheses are mutually exclusive.
A hazard probability model removes uncertainty so that communication of risk is simply stating one number.
